about: Findings that `bun run fuzz:ci` (seeds 1..500) still produces on master; test/fuzz/README.md explains the gate. Each entry names the open issue or PR that tracks it and lists the seeds it fires on. An entry matches a finding on status, errorName, the file of its top library frame and a message prefix, and only covers the seeds it lists: the same error on any other seed counts as new. Delete an entry when its fix lands; the run prints a note once an entry or some of its seeds stop reproducing.

findings.example: a recursive definition whose reference to itself carries a refining keyword, compiled with unreachableDefinitions: {"definitions": {"B": {"type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "string"}}, "additionalProperties": {"$ref": "#/definitions/B", "required": ["id"]}}}} with {unreachableDefinitions: true}. B is a concrete object type, but the error calls it a $ref cycle with no concrete base case; the same definition reached through a plain root-level $ref compiles. PR 840 (compose a $ref with sibling keywords as an intersection instead of a merged copy) compiles it, so the entry goes when that lands.

findings.message: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for '
findings.example: a boolean-schema definition referenced once plainly and once with a refining keyword beside the $ref: {"definitions": {"B": true}, "type": "object", "properties": {"c": {"$ref": "#/definitions/B"}, "a": {"$ref": "#/definitions/B", "required": ["id"]}}}. The ref parser caches `true` for the first reference and then evaluates `key in true` while merging the second one's siblings, so the error comes from inside @apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser (no library frame). Same family as issue 725; PR 840 no longer hands the ref parser a $ref with siblings and compiles it.
